ontology.api: louie::OntologyRegistry -- the widget type catalog, its per-type schemas, and the actions each type publishes

capabilities.name: query_ontology
capabilities.description: Return the ontology type catalog: every widget type an agent may encounter.

capabilities.name: get_schema
capabilities.description: Return the schema for one widget type: its properties and the actions it offers.

capabilities.name: get_tree
capabilities.description: Return a snapshot of the current UI tree.

capabilities.name: get_state
capabilities.description: Return the state of one widget, by its agent id.

capabilities.name: subscribe
capabilities.description: Begin receiving the named application events. Changes only the caller's own subscription set.

capabilities.name: unsubscribe
capabilities.description: Stop receiving the named application events.

capabilities.name: execute_action
capabilities.description: Invoke an action on a widget -- the primary way an agent drives the application.

capabilities.name: inject_event
capabilities.description: Synthesise an input event into the application, bypassing the widget action vocabulary.

note: Effects are read from the protocol's own semantics, not from a declared flag. The ontology here carries a `mutates` field, but it describes widget state -- whether clicking a control changes what the control shows -- which is a different question from whether an agent needs authority to do it. Mapping it would mark every button press as requiring a grant and say nothing useful. Grants go to the three operations that act on the application rather than describe it: execute_action, inject_event and quit. inject_event is granted separately from execute_action on purpose: execute_action is bounded by the action vocabulary a widget publishes, while inject_event synthesises raw input and is bounded by nothing the ontology declares. Nothing is budgeted. No operation's cost scales with a quantity the caller supplies; the event subscription is the only unbounded one, and its volume is set by the application's own event rate rather than by the request. Louie's protocol has no screenshot: a terminal frame is already text, and get_tree returns it as structure.
